Its invalid-cache fallback `(fn-cvec-record-debt (fn-sf-records (fn-sn-files s)))` -> fn-sfr-list -> fn-hrs-disk-history -> ... -> fn-hrs-fill-run -> fn-pgs-fill-realize, which re-takes *fnn-extent-lock* with a non-recursive with-mutex (host/native/extent.lisp:1717, :wait-p t) while limit-serialized already holds E: a recursive-lock error if ever reached. It is unreachable in steady state because the carried cache is set at install (owner-host.lisp:642-645) and by recovery (books/owner-recovery-retain.lisp:56-57), and the arm needs (consp cache), (car cache) <= count to fail. Not proven in ACL2 here; the valid-cache lemmas exist (fn-cvec-full-debt-cache-is-valid) but do not state that the arm is dead.
(2) O path: fn-host-hist-sync (host/store-node-host.lisp:101-106) takes the whole-history disk load (fn-hist-refresh with reload -> fn-sf-records -> disk pages -> fn-pgs-fill-realize preads) on the first call after an open (fn-store-sn-hist-reload set only by fn-store-sn-reset at open: store-open-host.lisp:601, store-write-host.lisp:1204). But history-root.lisp:96-99 returns before any row when fn-owner-hroot-begin does not answer :building. Then the first runtime fn-host-hist-sync (e.g. fnn-owner-inspect-request admin.lisp:394 -> fn-store-sn-lookup-foundp, store-node-host.lisp:1558; or the feed reply, owner-host.lisp:5355) loads the whole history from disk inside the owner quantum (O held; fill-realize does not hold E at the pread there). The fn-owner-install-profile fold (owner-host.lisp:640) reads fn-sf-records directly and does NOT sync the stobj, so it does not consume the flag.
